product_description: Triages inbound Gmail threads for a Strategic Partnership Manager: decides needs_reply vs low_confidence, assigns an urgency tier, and drafts two reply options. Runs once per new thread on gpt-4o-mini.

dimensions.name: H1: Classification Accuracy
dimensions.question: Does needs_reply vs low_confidence match content specificity, not message count or politeness?
dimensions.low: Generic/templated cold outreach marked needs_reply, or a genuine specific ask dismissed as low_confidence. Follow-up volume used as evidence of a real relationship.
dimensions.medium: Correct call but the distinction was close and the reasoning doesn't show why content specificity (not volume) drove it.
dimensions.high: needs_reply reserved for genuine asks/questions/opportunities tied to real specifics; low_confidence correctly catches generic pitches even when personalized.

dimensions.name: H2: Tier Sensibility
dimensions.question: Is today/week/fyi assigned by actual urgency in the thread, not by classification alone?
dimensions.low: Tier is arbitrary or defaults to "today" regardless of whether anything time-sensitive is stated.
dimensions.medium: Tier is plausible but doesn't clearly track a real deadline or urgency signal in the body.
dimensions.high: "today" only when a real deadline/urgency is stated; "week"/"fyi" otherwise, matching the thread's actual stakes.

dimensions.name: H3: Draft Actionability
dimensions.question: Do both drafts commit to one specific next step referencing a specific thread detail?
dimensions.low: Drafts are generic pleasantries ("thanks, I'll get back to you") with no reference to anything specific in the thread and no committed next step.
dimensions.medium: One draft is specific and actionable; the other lapses into generic filler.
dimensions.high: Both drafts reference a specific detail from the thread and each commits to one concrete next step, with distinct angles.

dimensions.name: Ho1: Why-Specificity
dimensions.question: Does "why" cite an actual specific detail from the thread, not a vague label?
dimensions.low: "why" is a vacuous restatement ("this seems important") with nothing tied to the thread's actual content.
dimensions.medium: "why" mentions the general topic but not the specific detail that actually drove the classification/tier.
dimensions.high: "why" names the concrete detail (a deadline, a number, a named ask) that justifies both the classification and the tier.

dimensions.name: Ha1: Draft Groundedness
dimensions.question: Do drafts avoid inventing commitments, numbers, or dates not present in the thread?
dimensions.low: Drafts state specific numbers, dates, or commitments that aren't supported by anything in the thread.
dimensions.medium: Drafts stay mostly grounded but include one vague filler claim not tied to the thread.
dimensions.high: Every specific claim in both drafts traces back to something actually in the thread; nothing fabricated.

test_cases.label: BAD
test_cases.input_description: Vendor sends a 3rd follow-up ("Quick call to discuss cutting costs?") with no reply to the prior two, generic cost-savings pitch.
test_cases.ground_truth: Should be low_confidence/fyi — generic templated pitch, follow-up volume is a cold-outreach signal, not evidence of a relationship.

evals.classification_accuracy: FAIL — marked needs_reply despite a generic "reduce costs" pitch with 3 unanswered follow-ups.
evals.tier_sensibility: FAIL — marked "today" with nothing time-sensitive stated.
evals.draft_actionability: FAIL — both drafts are generic pleasantries, no next step, no thread detail referenced.
evals.why_specificity: FAIL — why is "This seems like an important message that needs attention," no specific detail cited.
evals.draft_groundedness: PASS — doesn't fabricate anything, but only because it says nothing specific at all.

candidate_input.subject: Quick call to discuss cutting costs?
candidate_input.body: Hi Ellen, following up again — wanted to see if you had 15 minutes this week to explore how we've helped similar partnership teams reduce vendor costs by 20-30%. Let me know what works!

candidate_output.why: This seems like an important message that needs attention.

drafts.label: Friendly
drafts.text:
Hi Marcus,

Thanks for reaching out! I'll get back to you soon.

Best,
Ellen

drafts.label: Polite
drafts.text:
Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the note. Let me take a look and circle back.

Best,
Ellen

test_cases.label: AVERAGE
test_cases.input_type: Real prospect, wrong tier + thin why
test_cases.input_description: Prospect asks a specific pricing question tied to a named deck and seat count, but nothing in the thread is actually urgent.
test_cases.ground_truth: needs_reply is correct; tier should be week (nothing time-sensitive stated); why should cite the 400-seat/deck detail directly.

evals.classification_accuracy: PASS — correctly needs_reply given the specific 400-seat pricing ask.
evals.tier_sensibility: FAIL — marked "today" though nothing in the thread states urgency.
evals.draft_actionability: PARTIAL — one draft proposes a number and next step; the other is generic filler.
evals.why_specificity: PARTIAL — mentions "pricing" but not the 400-seat/deck detail that actually matters.
evals.draft_groundedness: PASS — no fabricated specifics beyond the thread.

candidate_input.subject: Following up on pricing tiers for 400 seats
candidate_input.body: Hi Ellen, following up on the deck you sent last week — could you confirm per-seat pricing and contract term length for a 400-employee rollout? Want to bring a number to our internal review.

drafts.label: Direct with numbers
drafts.text:
Hi Priya,

For 400 seats we're looking at a tiered rate depending on term length — I'll pull together both scenarios and send a number today.

Best,
Ellen

drafts.label: Follow up
drafts.text:
Hi Priya,

Thanks for reaching out, let me get back to you with details.

Best,
Ellen

test_cases.label: GOOD
test_cases.input_type: Real renewal ask with a stated deadline
test_cases.input_description: Existing contact asks to confirm pricing at two term lengths ahead of a named internal meeting on a specific day.
test_cases.ground_truth: needs_reply/today (real deadline stated); why should name the steering-committee deadline; both drafts should commit to one next step grounded in the 24mo/36mo ask.

evals.classification_accuracy: PASS — genuine specific ask from an existing contact.
evals.tier_sensibility: PASS — "today" justified by the stated Thursday steering-committee deadline.
evals.draft_actionability: PASS — both drafts commit to a specific next step tied to the term-length ask.
evals.why_specificity: PASS — names the Thursday deadline and the 24mo/36mo decision driving it.
evals.draft_groundedness: PASS — no numbers or commitments invented beyond what's implied by the ask.

candidate_input.subject: MSA renewal terms — 24mo vs 36mo
candidate_input.body: Hi Ellen, ahead of our steering committee on Thursday, could you confirm per-seat pricing for both the 24-month and 36-month renewal terms? Want to bring a clear recommendation into the meeting.

candidate_output.why: Marcus needs both term-length prices confirmed before Thursday's steering committee meeting.

drafts.text:

Best,
